title: Survey of Respiratory Motion Management Practices in Particle Therapy Facilities in Japan

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Survey of Respiratory Motion Management Practices in Particle Therapy Facilities in Japan》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-2】This study aimed to clarify the current implementation and technical trends of respiratory motion management in particle therapy in Japan.

【Abstract · abstract-1-5】The survey investigated treatment sites requiring respiratory motion management, CT datasets used for treatment planning, irradiation techniques, respiratory monitoring devices, gating phase determination methods, dose evaluation approaches, and patient positioning techniques.

evidence.text: This study aimed to clarify the current implementation and technical trends of respiratory motion management in particle therapy in Japan.

The survey investigated treatment sites requiring respiratory motion management, CT datasets used for treatment planning, irradiation techniques, respiratory monitoring devices, gating phase determination methods, dose evaluation approaches, and patient positioning techniques.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Survey of Respiratory Motion Management Practices in Particle Therapy Facilities in Japan》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-5】The survey investigated treatment sites requiring respiratory motion management, CT datasets used for treatment planning, irradiation techniques, respiratory monitoring devices, gating phase determination methods, dose evaluation approaches, and patient positioning techniques.

【Abstract · abstract-1-10】Determination of the irradiation phase based on tumor motion magnitude was the most commonly adopted approach (66.7%, 10/15), whereas some facilities used the same irradiation phase for all patients (20.0%, 3/15).

evidence.text: The survey investigated treatment sites requiring respiratory motion management, CT datasets used for treatment planning, irradiation techniques, respiratory monitoring devices, gating phase determination methods, dose evaluation approaches, and patient positioning techniques.

Determination of the irradiation phase based on tumor motion magnitude was the most commonly adopted approach (66.7%, 10/15), whereas some facilities used the same irradiation phase for all patients (20.0%, 3/15).
